programme_facts.value: The creative application of scientific principles to design or develop structures, machines, apparatus, or manufacturing processes, or works utilizing them singly or in combination; or to construct or operate the same with full cognizance of their design; or to forecast their behavior under specific operating conditions; all as respects an intended function, economics of operation and safety to life and property.
Engineering has existed since ancient times, when humans devised inventions such as the wedge, lever, wheel, and pulley.
The term engineering is derived from the word engineer, which dates back to the 14th century when an engine'er referred to 'a constructor of military engines'.
In this context, an 'engine' referred to a military machine, such as a catapult.
The term civil engineering entered the lexicon to distinguish between those specializing in the construction of non-military projects and those involved in military engineering.
The word 'engine' ultimately derives from the Latin ingenium, meaning 'innate quality, especially mental power, hence a clever invention.'

One who practices engineering is called an engineer.
Those licensed to practice engineering may have formal designations such as Professional Engineer, Chartered Engineer, Incorporated Engineer, Ingenieur, European Engineer.
A Designated Engineering Representative is an official title granted by the FAA.
Engineers apply mathematics and the physical sciences to find novel solutions to problems or to improve existing solutions.
Many engineers continue to learn new material throughout their careers.
Engineers weigh each design choice based on their merit and choose the solution that best matches the requirements.

Constraints may include the fundamental laws of physics and chemistry, available resources, physical, imaginative or technical limitations, flexibility for future modifications and additions, and other factors, such as requirements for cost, safety, marketability, productivity, and serviceability.
By understanding the constraints, engineers derive specifications for the limits within which a viable object or system may be produced and operated.
Computers and software play an increasingly important role in modern scientific and technological endeavors.
Typical business application software and computer-aided technologies are used specifically for engineering.
Computers can be used to generate models of fundamental physical processes, which can be solved using numerical methods.
One of the most widely used design tools in engineering is computer-aided design (CAD) software.
CAD enables engineers to create 3D models, 2D drawings, and schematics of their designs.

CAD, together with digital mockup (DMU) and computer-aided engineering (CAE) software allows engineers to create models of designs that can be analyzed without having to make expensive and time-consuming physical prototypes.

These tools allow products and components to be checked for flaws, assess fit and assembly, study ergonomics, and analyze static and dynamic characteristics of systems such as stresses, temperatures, electromagnetic emissions, electrical currents and voltages, digital logic levels, fluid flows, and kinematics.
Access and distribution of all this information is generally organized with the use of product data management software.
There are tools to support specific engineering tasks such as computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) software to generate CNC machining instructions.
Manufacturing process management software is used for production engineering.
Electronic design automation (EDA) is used for printed circuit board (PCB) and circuit schematics for electronic engineers.
MRO applications are used for maintenance management.
Architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) software is used for civil engineering.
The use of computer software to aid the development of goods has collectively come to be known as product lifecycle management (PLM).

Engineering is an important and learned profession. As members of this profession, engineers are expected to exhibit the highest standards of honesty and integrity. Engineering has a direct and vital impact on the quality of life for all people. Accordingly, the services provided by engineers require honesty, impartiality, fairness, and equity, and must be dedicated to the protection of the public health, safety, and welfare. Engineers must perform under a standard of professional behavior that requires adherence to the highest principles of ethical conduct.
